claim_as_stated: NCF Program Agreement (effective 2025-09-17) bans sharing credentials with third-party services, bans scraping, and states NCF does not authorize any third-party service to access the Secure Site.
exact_values_found: Heading 'Credential sharing prohibition, password security and notification': agree not to '(i) share your credentials with any third-party service, application, or individual ... (iv) authorize any third-party service or application to access the NCF charitable fund you established or the Secure Site on your behalf'; providing credentials to 'payment processors, financial aggregators, or charitable giving platforms' is a 'material breach'. Heading 'Third-party services': 'NCF does not authorize any third-party service to access the Secure Site or an NCF charitable fund on behalf of users.' Heading 'Scraping prohibition': bans bots/crawlers/scripts, bulk download, RPA 'regardless of whether such automation is used for convenience'. 'The foregoing Program Agreement is effective as of September 17, 2025.'
interpretation_challenge: Quote in repo is exact but truncated: the sentence continues 'or an NCF charitable fund on behalf of users'. The credential ban also covers advisors ('any third person (including advisors)') and MFA codes.

claim_as_stated: Vanguard Charitable User Agreement (May 2025) bars any 'electronic agent, bot' yet permits read-only aggregators run by the account holder; names 'grant recommendation processing services'.
exact_values_found: Password clause: 'you shall not allow any program, expert system, electronic agent, bot, or other automated means to access the Secure Site. You are prohibited from allowing another person or entity, including charities or grant recommendation processing services, to use your user name(s) and password(s)'. Aggregator clause: 'An Authorized Person may use "aggregators" or similar web crawler devices for the purpose of aggregating information regarding the Donor-Advised Account(s)...'; Vanguard 'may prevent in its discretion, the systematic, commercial or otherwise inappropriate use' of automated devices; 'Unauthorized Third Parties are not permitted to use aggregators'. An Unauthorized Third Party is any third party using an Authorized Person's credentials.
discrepancies: 'read-only' does not appear in the text; the permission is for 'aggregators or similar web crawler devices' used 'for the purpose of aggregating information'. The permission is to the Authorized Person, not to an aggregator service; a hosted aggregator using the donor's credentials is by definition an 'Unauthorized Third Party'.
contradictory_evidence: Same agreement bars 'any program ... electronic agent, bot, or other automated means' from accessing the Secure Site, and reserves discretion to block 'systematic, commercial' automated access.
interpretation_challenge: 'Read-only aggregators run by the account holder' is a fair gloss of purpose, but should be presented as inference, not quoted text; practically only self-run tools qualify.

claim_as_stated: NPT Terms of Use (2026-10-29) ban robot harvesting and use of site data to build AI tools.
exact_values_found: (v) 'collecting or scraping data about other users or harvesting data from the Site using robots, spiders, scripts, software or any manual or automatic device, tool or process to populate databases or collect Site Content, data or information for any purpose'; (viii) 'using the Site Content or any user data for the development of any software program, model, algorithm or generative artificial intelligence ("AI") tool, including but not limited to training, fine tuning or otherwise using the Site Content or user data in connection with the development or operation of a machine learning or AI system'.
interpretation_challenge: Clause (viii) is broader than 'build AI tools': it also covers 'operation' of an ML/AI system and any 'software program, model, algorithm'. Terms of Use and Privacy Policy are one combined page (nptrust.org/?p=3 redirects to /privacy-policy/).

claim_as_stated: Fidelity Charitable License Agreement s.8 provides for export to third-party software.
exact_values_found: '8. ACCOUNT EXPORT OR DOWNLOAD TO THIRD PARTY PRODUCTS OR ON-LINE SERVICES: Fidelity Charitable may provide users the opportunity to export or download Giving Account information via electronic transmission, to a personal computer and display the information within a third party software product or on-line service.' Data received by the third-party product 'becomes the sole responsibility of the user'.
contradictory_evidence: s.1 limits the licence to computers in the household and a single workplace computer; ECSA bars making electronic services 'available to any third parties'. No live Fidelity help page documenting such a third-party export was found.
interpretation_challenge: s.8 is permissive ('may provide'), not a donor right or a commitment that a third-party export exists today; the agreement is undated and the clause reads as legacy (Quicken-era) boilerplate.

claim_as_stated: AEF's live FAQ shows a DonorCentral 'Export' button.
exact_values_found: 'Q. How do I generate a list of grants paid within a specific date range?' ... 'Click on the Export button, and the file will automatically be exported to the device's Download location.' Sits under 'How to Access Your Grant Documents in DonorCentral' on the 'AEF TECHNOLOGY UPGRADE' (Ren platform) support site.
contradictory_evidence: Same page trains donors on the new Ren-powered platform ('how Ren defines roles'); a search-index summary of AEF's FAQ says only 2024-2025 and 2026 history will be reviewable on the new platform and donors should 'visit DonorCentral to obtain the rest of your account history' (not visible on the fetched page).
interpretation_challenge: The Export is scoped to a grants-paid list in the legacy DonorCentral, published in a migration context; it does not show a full-ledger or ongoing export on AEF's new platform. File format not stated.

claim_as_stated: Candid API licence (2026-09-14) bars redistribution and AI extraction and requires stopping all use on termination; Charity Check sources include Pub78, BMF, IRB, revocations and OFAC SDN.
exact_values_found: 3.b.ii: may not 'republish or distribute information from the Candid API ... except as expressly permitted herein'; 3.b.v same 'except as permitted herein and in the Order Form'; 3.a.i permits providing Candid Data to Licensee Customers via the Licensee Site. 3.b.xi: no data mining/robots/extraction to (1) compile a nonprofit database 'other than for Licensee's own internal business use', (2) license/sell such a database, or (3) build a directly competitive service; 'This prohibition expressly applies to data mining or extraction for use in or through the use of artificial intelligence ("A.I."), large language models, machine learning'. Termination: 'Licensee shall cease, and shall cause its Authorized Users to cease, all use of the Candid Data'. Charity Check FAQ: EO BMF, Tax Exempt Organization Search (Pub78), Automatic Revocation List, IRB, OFAC SDN List; getting-started page lists the same five.
discrepancies: 'Bars AI extraction' overstates clause xi: the AI language qualifies a prohibition scoped to building databases beyond internal business use, reselling, or competing with Candid; AI use of Candid Data for a licensee's internal business use is not expressly barred. 'Bars redistribution' omits that distribution to Licensee Customers through the Licensee Site and per the Order Form is permitted.
contradictory_evidence: Developer-portal Candid License Agreement (Dec 2023) carries similar AI language: older form.
interpretation_challenge: Repo body text (sec.5 table) quotes clause xi correctly; the P-QA2-07 summary bullets ('expressly bars extraction for artificial intelligence'; 'bars republication') drop the scope qualifiers.
